title: User API errors during morning peak
executive_summary: INC-009 (SEV2, user API errors during the morning peak, affecting api-gateway and user-service) is assessed as ROOT_CAUSE_IDENTIFIED. The leading hypothesis (H1, confidence 0.855) is a deployment regression: user-service 7.1.3 to 7.2.0 (ORM switch to batch loader, deployed 07:56Z, SUCCEEDED) introduced a defect in ProfileBatchLoader that throws NullPointerExceptions and returns HTTP 500s on GET /v1/users/{id} (dep-c02e51b7, logpat-user-service-2347725d). Error rate on user-service rose from a baseline of about 0.41% to a window mean of 13.43% (max 26.11%) starting 07:57Z, and p95 latency rose from about 80 ms to about 410 ms (max 754 ms) (met-user-service-error_rate-0730-0900, met-user-service-p95_latency_ms-0730-0900). API gateway 5xx responses from user-service began at 07:57:09Z (logpat-api-gateway-c1d874f7). Request rate, CPU and DB connection utilisation stayed flat, which points away from load and connection-pool exhaustion. Alternative hypotheses were rejected: a slow postgres report query (H2) and a notification-service traffic surge (H3). The conclusion is the most probable explanation, not a confirmed fact. Log coverage was partial for all queries.

critic_review.summary: H1 (user-service 7.2.0 ProfileBatchLoader defect) is well supported and consistent in time. The 7.1.3->7.2.0 deploy at 07:56 (SUCCEEDED, the only config/deploy change in the window) precedes the user-service error_rate and p95 onset at 07:57. A fresh log query, though partial, returned NPEs in ProfileBatchLoader.load tagged v7.2.0 starting 07:58:29, which resolves the earlier 08:00:53 vs 07:59:37 discrepancy: the earlier 08:00:53 timestamp came from a partial log set. Gateway 500s from user-service begin 07:57:09, matching. Request rate (+1.1%), CPU, and DB connection utilisation are flat, so load and pool exhaustion are contradicted. H2 is rejected: postgres p95 latency and connection utilisation are flat, and user-service errors are application NPEs rather than DB errors. H3 is rejected: notification-service request rate is flat and user-service total load is unchanged. The config-change query returned nothing for the window.

assessments.reasoning: Deploy at 07:56 precedes error and p95 onset at 07:57. Version-tagged NPEs in ProfileBatchLoader.load appear from 07:58:29 onward. Gateway 500s track from 07:57:09. Load, CPU, and DB pool metrics are flat, which fits a code-path defect. Unverified: the per-instance rollout and the exact retry mechanism behind the p95 rise. These are minor and do not change the culprit.

Postgres p95 latency (12.0 vs 12.0 ms) and connection utilisation (~40%) are flat across the window. The slow report_rollup statements predate and do not align with the user-service onset. User-service failures are NPEs in application code, not DB errors.

Notification-service request rate is flat (+1.1%). User-service total request rate and CPU are flat, so there is no overload. The topology edge dates from 09-15 with no change, and no log or metric links notification-service to the failures.

corrective_actions: Roll back user-service from 7.2.0 to 7.1.3 (the last known-good version) to restore error rate and latency, then confirm recovery in error_rate and p95 metrics.
Verify the rollback on all instances, since per-instance deployment state was not confirmed (critic assumption).
Check whether api-gateway retries or circuit breakers are masking or amplifying failures, and keep the rollback under observation until the 5xx rate returns to baseline (about 0.5%).
preventive_actions: Fix the null-handling defect in ProfileBatchLoader.load for the 7.2.0 code path and add regression tests covering null or missing profile inputs on GET /v1/users/{id}.
Gate the ORM and batch-loader change behind a canary or feature flag with automated error-rate and latency rollback thresholds before full rollout.
Require pre-production load and error-path testing for data-access layer changes.
Improve deployment traceability by recording per-instance rollout state and version tags on all log lines.

conclusion: The most probable root cause of INC-009 is the user-service 7.2.0 deployment, specifically a NullPointerException defect in ProfileBatchLoader that produces 500 errors and latency growth on GET /v1/users/{id}, which propagate to api-gateway. The timing of the deploy, error and latency onset, and log signatures all support this. Load, database connection pool and postgres contention were ruled out. Rollback to 7.1.3 is the priority mitigation, and a defect fix with canary gating is the long-term remedy.
